topic: Force majeure lifted and full project restart (2025-2026)
wiki_text: On 7 November 2025 the Mozambique LNG consortium, operated by TotalEnergies, decided to lift the force majeure declared in April 2021 following insurgent attacks in Cabo Delgado. On 29 January 2026 Mozambique LNG announced the full restart of all onshore and offshore activities at the Afungi site, with more than 4,000 workers mobilized (over 3,000 Mozambican nationals). The company stated the project was about 40% complete (most engineering and procurement of main equipment executed during the force majeure period) and is now targeting first LNG in 2029 on a revised budget (~US$20 billion) and schedule. Partners agreed to provide additional equity to support the restart. The Area 1 venture is TotalEnergies (26.5%, operator), Mitsui (20%), ENH (15%), Bharat PetroResources/BPRL (10%), Oil India (10%), ONGC Videsh (10%) and PTTEP (8.5%).

topic: Final investment decision and JV restructuring (Oct 2025)
wiki_text: On 2 October 2025 Eni and partners announced the final investment decision for the Coral North FLNG project, a second floating LNG unit developing the northern part of Area 4's Coral reservoir in the Rovuma basin, offshore Cabo Delgado. The FLNG has a liquefaction capacity of 3.6 MTPA and is targeted for delivery in 2028; together with Coral South it would lift Mozambique's LNG output above 7 MTPA. The hull was launched on 16 January 2026 at Geoje, South Korea. The project is implemented by a joint venture of Eni (50%), CNPC (20%), Kogas (10%), ENH (10%) and ADNOC's subsidiary XRG (10%); ExxonMobil is not a partner in the Coral North FLNG vehicle. The project is projected to generate about US$23 billion in tax revenues and US$3 billion in local contracts.

topic: Force majeure lifted; revised 18 MTPA modular design; FID expected 2026
wiki_text: ExxonMobil lifted force majeure on the Area 4 onshore Rovuma LNG project around 20 November 2025 as Cabo Delgado security improved, targeting a final investment decision in 2026 and first LNG by about 2030. The project was redesigned from two 7.6 MTPA trains (15.2 MTPA) to twelve modular, electric-driven trains of 1.5 MTPA each, for a total of roughly 18 MTPA, to speed delivery and reduce execution risk and emissions. ExxonMobil leads onshore liquefaction; Eni leads upstream. Partners include ExxonMobil, Eni, CNPC, ADNOC's XRG, Kogas and ENH. EPC (onshore) and upstream FEED contracts were awarded in November 2024.

topic: Government approval of two state-led FSRU import terminals (Nov 2025)
wiki_text: On 25 November 2025 Mozambique approved two FSRU-based LNG import terminals to be anchored at the Port of Beira and at Inhambane (Inhassoro area), connected to domestic gas pipelines under a 30-year concession. The concession is to be managed through a special-purpose vehicle formed by state-owned entities — ENH, Mozambique's Ports and Railways (CFM), the electricity utility EDM and the Cahora Bassa hydro company (HCB) — together with government-selected partners with technical and financial capacity. Specific capacities and private partners were not disclosed at approval.
